purpose: Implement overturn_protocol arm c22 (scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit with a gap) as a real runner (blueprints/gap-resolution-20260922/sklearn-timeseriessplit/run_c22.py) and execute it on the SAME frozen blueprints/us-equities/research-evaluation/plan.json inputs (sha256 b8d1beba6eddd0388957ca0d9e9c46ebfb2ca538f076419d5a8dcaaaf82be4a7) using the SAME unmodified label/selection/cost helper functions imported from evaluate.py, so only the splitter differs from the accepted skfolio WalkForward receipt. This directly answers the critic's correction that the prior proposed check installed scikit-learn but never implemented or ran a TimeSeriesSplit runner.
preregistered: Fixed before running: report, for both arms side by side, (a) development fold count, (b) total ledger record count, (c) the reserved-2021Q1 chosen candidate, and (d) that candidate's reserved mean_net_cost_proxy_label. A result counts as 'matches skfolio' only if (c) and (d) are identical between arms; a different chosen candidate or a materially different net-of-cost mean would be a genuine divergence. It is also expected, and reported honestly either way, that scikit-learn's TimeSeriesSplit has no reduce_test equivalent, so (a)/(b) may differ from skfolio's WalkForward even if (c)/(d) match, because the reserved-segment window in both scripts is computed directly from plan.json (eligible[-(train_size+purge):-purge]), independent of which development-fold splitter is used -- so an identical (c)/(d) result would demonstrate the reserved conclusion is not an artifact of skfolio's specific splitter, not that the two splitters produce identical development folds.

result: Side-by-side comparison, reserved 2021Q1 segment: skfolio WalkForward (from the accepted receipt, reproduced this run: 20 development folds, 6605 ledger records) and scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit(max_train_size=252, test_size=63, gap=6) (19 development folds, 6300 ledger records, since TimeSeriesSplit has no reduce_test tail-trim) both select momentum20 as the reserved candidate with an IDENTICAL mean_net_cost_proxy_label of 0.001184071666615635470939591764 (0.118407%...). This equality is structurally expected, not coincidental: both scripts compute the reserved train/test window directly from plan.json rather than from either splitter's fold output, so the reserved-segment result is invariant to which development-cross-validation engine is used. The development-fold counts genuinely differ (19 vs 20) because scikit-learn's TimeSeriesSplit has no equivalent to skfolio's reduce_test=True tail behavior; this is a real, reported difference between the two libraries, not an error.

verdict_impact.explanation: This is the first executed comparison between skfolio and any other candidate on the frozen research-evaluation inputs (closing part of gap 6 in both layers): a second, independently-implemented splitter engine (scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit) reaches the same reserved-segment conclusion as skfolio's WalkForward, which supports (does not overturn) skfolio's reserved result as not being a splitter-specific artifact. It does not settle the gap fully: it only compares splitters, not skfolio against a full competing factor/model library (sktime, alphalens, Qlib remain uncached and out of reach offline per the triage), and the development-fold count difference (19 vs 20, no reduce_test in scikit-learn) is a genuine, reportable divergence between the two libraries' walk-forward semantics.

limitations: Only compares the WalkForward/TimeSeriesSplit splitter layer, not a full alternative factor/model/feature library (sktime, alphalens-reloaded, statsmodels, arch, tsfresh, river, statsforecast, chronos, timesfm, Qlib remain source-review only per the triage; none were cached offline).

The reserved-segment metric equality is partly a property of both scripts' shared plan.json-derived reserved window rather than a property of the splitters converging on the development folds; the development fold/ledger counts do differ (19 vs 20 folds, 6300 vs 6605 records).

run_c22.py imports evaluate.py's unmodified label/choose/summaries/verify_inputs/load_panel functions rather than reimplementing them, so this arm is not a fully independent reimplementation of the labeling logic -- it isolates the splitter as the only varying component by design, which is what overturn_protocol's c22 asked for, but it is not a from-scratch second implementation.
